actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species ranges from central Ethiopia, Djibouti and Somalia south through eastern Kenya to extreme northeast Tanzania (Wüster and Broadley 2007, Spawls et al. 2002). The distribution map provided by Wüster and Broadley (2007) suggests that it may also occur in the extreme southeast of South Sudan, but no records are available for this country. Within this area it is widespread, although only a small number of Tanzanian records are known (Spawls et al. 2002, Wüster and Broadley 2003). It occurs from sea level to around 1,200 m asl (Spawls et al. 2018).
documentation.population: Ineich (2001) tentatively considers the species common in Djibouti, based on the frequency of reports, however it's not clear whether these records include specimens now referred to Naja nubiae (which has been confirmed from Assab in Eritrea close to Djibouti). This is a common species in parts of Kenya (S. Spawls pers. comm. 2014). Targeted searches for these cobras at known Tanzanian localities can reliably find at least one animal a day (J. Beraduccii pers. comm. 2014). It is probably quite common in Ethiopia (S. Spawls pers. comm.). There is no evidence of decline at least in East Africa (J. Beraduccii pers. comm. 2014), outside areas where heavy development excludes the snake (P. Malonza pers. comm. 2014).
documentation.habitats: This is a terrestrial, primarily nocturnal cobra of dry savanna and semi-desert, although it may climb into bushes and low trees (Spawls et al. 2002), as well as arid grasslands (J. Beraduccii pers. comm. 2014). It feeds largely on amphibians, and can be encountered close to human habitations searching for water (Spawls et al. 2002). Other prey items include rodents and birds, and snakes will sometimes prey on domestic chickens (Spawls et al. 2002). Clutches consist of 6-15 eggs (Spawls et al. 2012).
documentation.threats: This species is under no widespread threat, although there are localized pressures from human encroachment and settlement.
documentation.measures: Records of this species exist for Tsavo National Park (Kenya) and Mkomazi Game Reserve (Tanzania), and Awash, Omo and Nech'sar National Parks in Ethiopia.
documentation.use_trade: There is no significant demand for this species in trade or for antivenom production, and it is not of interest to the international pet trade (J. Beraduccii pers. comm. 2014).
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern on the basis that this species is widespread in northeastern Africa, is subject to at most localized threats, and is regularly encountered with no evidence of decline.
